body.justification: The remaining mathematical target is to remove the proved at-most-\(\log(ed)\) gap on the unchanged observational class and determine which candidate elbows are genuine.
body.gap: No verified argument yet controls the coupled mass-weighted treated--control moment process uniformly over the Lipschitz dual class, and the existing same-class lower families do not select the sharp interpolation.
body.consumer: A solved frontier would calibrate categorical-profile CATE-law reporting without asserting individual treatment-effect recovery or point identification of a zero atom.

obligation.what_is_open: Remove the remaining at-most-\(\log(ed)\) factor, determine which displayed benchmark elbows are genuine, fully instantiate a measurable probability-valued grouped estimator, and prove a matching converse on the unchanged model class.
obligation.obstruction: Arbitrary unknown cell masses, null cells, tied effects, and unequal propensities at both overlap boundaries remain legal.  The deterministic mass-weighted Lipschitz extension does not control the supremum over all Lipschitz tests of the joint grouped factorial-moment error, while the scalar-transfer and separated-atom lower families certify different obstructions without determining their sharp interpolation.
obligation.attempted: The established route gives the total empirical upper bound, the normalized categorical scalar transfer, the separated-atom hypercube lower bound, and the exact dense frontier.  The algebraic comparison added here compresses these results to an at-most-logarithmic characterization and locates four candidate phases.  Summing cellwise errors recovers only the empirical upper benchmark; the candidate grouped blueprint still lacks a uniform covariance argument, optimized tuning, and a matching intermediate lower family.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved same-class characterization is
\[
 c_\epsilon L_{n,d}\leq R_{n,d,\epsilon}
 \leq C_\epsilon\log(ed)L_{n,d},
\]
where
\[
 L_{n,d}=\max\!\left\{
 \min\!\left(1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right),
 \min\!\left(\frac dn,n^{-2/3}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
For \(n>1\), its four branches are \(d/n\), \(n^{-2/3}\), \(d/[n\log(ed)]\), and \(1\), separated respectively by \(d=n^{1/3}\), \(d=n^{1/3}\log(ed)\), and \(d=n\log(ed)\).  The first branch is exactly the regime \(n\geq d^3\), where the same-class lower and empirical upper bounds match at order \(d/n\).  The empirical estimator continues to give the concrete bound \(C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/n\}\) on every two-effect-cluster subfamily with unknown unequal masses and propensities at either overlap boundary, without deleting null cells.  The existing bracket also yields the proved sufficient and necessary consistency conditions and the exact bounded-category parametric-risk boundary, but it does not decide the exact consistency region or the genuine sparse and transitional elbows.
